**Finding resubmitted: compliant** — no redline, no comment.

Summary of the repair: the substance of the finding is unchanged (it was the correct handling), with the rationale now explicitly recording two points the verifier surfaced:

1. **Why the deterministic check fails.** The "audit frequency limited" check fails because there is no audit clause at all to carry a frequency limit — not because of defective drafting. It signals no unaddressed risk.
2. **Why no wording is proposed.** Silence on Vendor audit rights sits above the AUDIT preferred position for us. Drafting in frequency/notice/cost parameters would manufacture a right against ourselves, so this is neither a deviation nor a "missing" clause requiring a redline.

Supporting record retained: §6 (documentation on request plus right to contest charges) and §3(e) (real-time usage statistics and raw log files) run in our favour; §8(f) (anti-spam technical mechanisms) and §9 (access for Y2K repairs at TrueLink's sole cost) are narrow, self-funded Vendor rights rather than usage audits, and create no frequency, notice, cost or system-access exposure. I have also noted the fallback posture for future negotiation, should TrueLink ever request an audit right.
